summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: most Hindi videos get 1,000+ views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly gets under 100 views. The best videos are about robots and 'surprising' sensor facts (gyro robot, clap switch, PIR sensor) with a bold hook that says the device lacks something obvious. Everyday-object videos (lifts, taps, smoke alarms, doors, touchscreens) and 'Kaise...?' explainers are weak, and the one English video got no Instagram reach.
winningPattern: Maker/robot or hobby-sensor subject (gyro, clap switch, PIR, line follower, mic) + a contrarian 'it can't X, it only Y' or 'without Z it falls' hook in casual Hinglish + short punchy title with one emoji, posted mainly for Instagram Reels where saves and shares come from relatable maker projects. Titles that say 'Nahi' or give a surprising claim beat plain 'Kaise Kaam Karta Hai?' questions.
doMore: Make robot and Arduino-module videos with a visible, demo-able result (falls, follows, reacts)
Open with a contrarian claim: 'X ko Y nahi pata, sirf Z pata hai'
Prioritise Instagram: post there first and add a save-worthy line like 'Save kar lo project ke liye'
Post more of the proven winners: clap switch, gyro, mic, line follower variations
Test one YouTube-specific change (stronger first-second visual, shorter title) since YT is stuck under 100 views
stopDoing: Generic 'Kaise Kaam Karta Hai? 🤔' titles on everyday objects like taps, doors, lifts
Publishing near-duplicate topics (two smoke detector, two IR sensor, two tap videos) in the same week
Mixing in English narration videos until Hindi is fully tested
